messages.subject: Simulating data with a simple CMR model
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to switch from JAGS to nimble and I am encountering troubles when simulating data from a simple, non-spatial, CMR model. I get a lot of "Dynamic index out of bounds" warnings and the simulated data are full of NaN. The model is so simple that I must be doing something obviously wrong but I cannot find what. Here is my code below. Can someone advise how to have the code running? Many thanks!

Guillaume

library(nimble)

##########################################################
# NIMBLE MODEL
##########################################################

simCode <- nimbleCode({
 
  # Observations O
  # 1 : seen alive
  # 2 : seen newly dead
  # 3 : not seen (can be alive or dead)
 
  po[1,1] <- pd       # Pr(alive t -> seen-alive t)
  po[1,2] <- 0        # Pr(alive t -> seen-dead t)
  po[1,3] <- 1 - pd   # Pr(alive t -> not-seen t)
 
  po[2,1] <- 0        # Pr(dead t -> seen-alive t)
  po[2,2] <- pd       # Pr(dead t -> seen-dead t)
  po[2,3] <- 1 - pd   # Pr(dead t -> not-seen t)
 
  po[3,1] <- 0        # Pr(dead-before t -> seen-alive t)
  po[3,2] <- 0        # Pr(dead-before t -> seen-dead t)
  po[3,3] <- 1        # Pr(dead-before t -> not-seen t)
 
  # States X
  # 1 : alive
  # 2 : newly dead
  # 3 : dead (before)
 
  px[1,1] <- phi            # Pr(alive t -> alive t+1)
  px[1,2] <- 1 - phi        # Pr(alive t -> dead t+1)
  px[1,3] <- 0              # Pr(alive t -> dead-before t+1)
 
  px[2,1] <- 0              # Pr(dead t -> alive t+1)
  px[2,2] <- 0              # Pr(dead t -> dead t+1)
  px[2,3] <- 1              # Pr(dead t -> dead-before t+1)
 
  px[3,1] <- 0              # Pr(dead-before t -> alive t+1)
  px[3,2] <- 0              # Pr(dead-before t -> dead t+1)
  px[3,3] <- 1              # Pr(dead-before t -> dead-before t+1)
 
 
  # Priors
  phi ~ dunif(0,1) # prior on phi1
  pd ~ dunif(0,1)  # prior on detection probability
 
  # Likelihood
  for (i in 1:N) {
   
    # Latent state at entry
    z[i,first[i]] <- y[i,first[i]]
   
    for (t in (first[i]+1):Y) {
     
      # draw z(t) given z(t-1)
      z[i,t] ~ dcat(px[z[i,t-1], 1:3])
     
      # draw y(t) given z(t)
      y[i,t] ~ dcat(po[z[i,t], 1:3])
     
    }
   
  }
 
})

##########################################################
# PREPARE CONSTANTS AND INITS
##########################################################

n.years <- 10
n.animals <- 20

first.year <- rep(1, n.animals) # For simplicity, animals all enter at year 1

##########################################################
# MODEL
##########################################################

simModel <- nimbleModel(code = simCode,
                        constants = list(N = n.animals, Y = n.years, first = first.year),
                        inits = list(phi = 0.8, pd = 0.6))

# simModel$calculate('y')

nodesToSim <- simModel$getDependencies(c("phi", "pd"), self = T, downstream = T)
nodesToSim

simModel$simulate(nodesToSim)
simModel$y

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Simulating data with a simple CMR model
parts:
Dear Giullaume,
Thanks for the question and welcome to nimble.
From reading your code, it looks to me that a problem could arise because you have not provided initial values for y[i, first[i]].
The "dynamic index" is very likely referring to z[i, t] (and z[i, t-1]) values, since those are random (dynamic) variables used as indices. It looks like z[i, first[i]] will be NA, because y[i, first[i]] has not been initialized, and then the entire sequence of z[i, t] values won't make sense. You can provide an inits matrix for y that has only the first column populated and leave other values as NA.
You've already seen that you can inspect variables by simModel$z, etc.
HTH!
Perry

The inits got rid of the error, thank you!

I pass these simulated data to be fitted by MCMC. I am careful to well initialise the latent state, by telling animals are assumed alive if not observed before their possible death, and assumed dead when not observed after their death. The model runs fine and I have no warnings that I could get before running log of infinite density. The chains look well mixed and the parameters have narrow distributions.

However, and to my surprise, I don't recover at all the parameters I used to simulate the data. Detection probability was at 0.6 and I get 0.26 back, survival probability was at 0.8 and I get 0.93 back. I have increased sample size to 100 animals observed during 20 years but I still cannot recover the parameters used for the simulation. Aren't the same parameter values supposed to be recovered or is there a particular trick to be able to do so? Thank you!

##########################################################
# PREPARE CONSTANTS
##########################################################

n.years <- 20
n.animals <- 100
phi <- 0.8
pd <- 0.6
first.year <- rep(1, n.animals) # For simplicity, animals all enter at year 1

simModel <- nimbleModel(code = simCode,
                        constants = list(N = n.animals, Y = n.years, first = first.year),

inits = list(phi = phi, pd = pd, y = yinits))

nodesToSim <- simModel$getDependencies(c("phi", "pd"), self = F, downstream = T)
nodesToSim

simModel$simulate(nodesToSim)
simModel$y

##########################################################
# FIT SIMULATED DATA
##########################################################

the.data <- list(y = simModel$y)

parameters.to.save <- c("phi",
                        "pd",
                        "po",
                        "px")

zinits <- simModel$y

# Re-code non-detections as alive or dead before (for true state z inits)
for (i in 1:n.animals) {
 
  if (2 %in% zinits[i,]) {
    year.death <- which(zinits[i,] == 2)
    if (year.death < n.years) {
      zinits[i,(year.death+1):n.years] <- 3 # re-code as dead before
    }
    zinits[i,1:(year.death-1)] <- 1 # re-code as alive
  } else {
    zinits[i,zinits[i,] == 3] <- 1 # re-code as alive if never found dead
  }
}

initial.values <- function() list(phi = runif(1, 0, 1),
                                  pd = runif(1, 0, 1),
                                  z = zinits)

the.constants = list(N = n.animals, Y = n.years, first = first.year)

n.iter <- 5000
n.burnin <- 1000
n.chains <- 2

fitModel <- nimbleMCMC(code = simCode,
                        data = the.data,
                        constants = the.constants,
                        inits = initial.values,
                        monitors = parameters.to.save,
                        niter = n.iter,
                        nburnin = n.burnin,
                        nchains = n.chains)

MCMCsummary(fitModel, params = parameters.to.save, round = 2)
MCMCplot(fitModel)

plot(fitModel[[1]][ , 'phi'], type = 'l', xlab = 'iteration',  ylab = expression(phi), col="blue")
lines(fitModel[[2]][ , 'phi'], type = 'l', col="red")

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Simulating data with a simple CMR model
parts:
Dear Guillaume,
I've run and studied your code for a few minutes.
It looks like your model is not amenable to valid MCMC updating by univariate samplers, due to the combination of latent state 2 moving deterministically to latent state 3 and latent state 1 never moving directly to latent state 3. Say z[i, t] is 2, which necessarily means z[i, t-1] is 1 and z[i, t+1] is 3. The categorical sampler will consider setting z[i, t] to 1 or 3, but both will be impossible (returning probability 0, i.e. log probability -Inf). If z[i, t] is updated to 1 or 3, then there would be a transition from state 1 to state 3 (at the next or previous time step, respectively), which has probability 0. As a result, if newly-dead was never observed, the MCMC will not mix over the unknown time of death. Wherever the 2s have been set in zinits will be locked in and not mix. This is not a flaw in nimble. The samplers are working correctly, but the model is constrained such that they can't explore the unknown z elements in the way you want. I think monitoring 'z' will reveal this.
You could use the hidden Markov model distributions in the nimbleEcology package. These will marginalize over the latent states and should I believe work correctly even for a model with your constraints. Alternatively it would be possible to write a sampler that updates neighboring z[i, t:(t+1)] pairs (or longer sequences) while maintaining the constraint, although that would be a little more involved.
A final note is that, in general for these kinds of models, for elements of z that are completely known, you can provide those as data, which will avoid having MCMC samplers needlessly try to update them.
HTH
Perry

  px[2,3] <- 1              # Pr(dead t -> dead-before t+1)
 
  px[3,1] <- 0              # Pr(dead-before t -> alive t+1)
  px[3,2] <- 0              # Pr(dead-before t -> dead t+1)
  px[3,3] <- 1              # Pr(dead-before t -> dead-before t+1)
 
 
  # Priors
  phi ~ dunif(0,1) # prior on phi1
  pd ~ dunif(0,1)  # prior on detection probability
 
  # Likelihood
  for (i in 1:N) {
   
    # Latent state at entry
    z[i,first[i]] <- y[i,first[i]]
   
    for (t in (first[i]+1):Y) {
     
      # draw z(t) given z(t-1)
      z[i,t] ~ dcat(px[z[i,t-1], 1:3])
     
      # draw y(t) given z(t)
      y[i,t] ~ dcat(po[z[i,t], 1:3])
     
    }
   
  }
 
})

##########################################################
# PREPARE CONSTANTS AND INITS
##########################################################

n.years <- 10
n.animals <- 20

first.year <- rep(1, n.animals) # For simplicity, animals all enter at year 1

##########################################################
# MODEL
##########################################################

simModel <- nimbleModel(code = simCode,
                        constants = list(N = n.animals, Y = n.years, first = first.year),
                        inits = list(phi = 0.8, pd = 0.6))

# simModel$calculate('y')

nodesToSim <- simModel$getDependencies(c("phi", "pd"), self = T, downstream = T)
nodesToSim

simModel$simulate(nodesToSim)
simModel$y
